product_name: Hartz® Flea Control Capsules™ / Zodiac® Fleatrol Flea Caps™

indication.text: Prevention and control of flea populations in dogs nine weeks of age and older and 4 pounds or more (insect growth regulator; inhibits flea egg development, does not kill adult fleas).
indication.quote: ZODIAC® FLEATROL™ FLEA CAPS™ and HARTZ® Flea Control Capsules™ are indicated for use in dogs, nine weeks of age and older and 4 pounds body weight or greater, for the prevention and control of flea populations.

dose_regimen.dose: 10 mg (S)-Methoprene per pound of body weight (22 mg/kg) minimum
dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: given according to a body-weight capsule schedule (1-4 capsules of 154/308/462 mg)
dose_regimen.quote: The capsules are given orally once per week at the recommended minimum dosage of 10 mg (S)-Methoprene per pound of body weight (22 mg/kg) according to the following schedule.

target_animal_safety.duration: once weekly for 13 weeks (1X, 3X, 5X; 90-day study); 10X once weekly for 4 weeks (28 days)

findings.finding: No adverse effects on body weight, food consumption, ophthalmology, clinical pathology, urinalysis, organ weights, gross pathology or histology; clinical signs were depression, ataxia and tremors.
findings.quote: There were no adverse effects on body weight, food consumption, ophthalmology, clinical pathology, urinalyses, organ weights, gross pathology or histology. The clinical signs included depression, ataxia (loss of balance) and tremors.

findings.finding: Depression, ataxia and tremors occurred at 1X, 3X, 5X and 10X in 6-week-old puppies (all returned to normal by the next observation).
findings.quote: (S)-Methoprene capsules caused clinical signs including depression, ataxia and tremors when administered at 1X, 3X, 5X and 10X the recommended dose in 6 week old puppies.

findings.finding: Depression recurred on days 0 and 7 in two 3X dogs and one 10X dog; by day 14 only one dog showed mild depression.
findings.quote: Two dogs in the 3x treatment group and 1 in the 10x group exhibited depression twice on days 0 and 7. By day 14 only 1 dog exhibited mild depression.

findings.finding: Conclusion: safe up to 5X the recommended dose in puppies 9 weeks of age and older and 4 pounds or more.
findings.quote: (S)-Methoprene capsules (22 mg/kg), administered up to 5X the recommended dose, are safe for administration to puppies, 9 weeks of age and older and 4 pounds body weight or greater.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: 32 Beagle puppies (16 males and 16 females), approximately 6-weeks old, 1.62-2.10 kg body weight. Groups 1-4 (6/group) and Groups 5 and 6 (4/group), divided equally by sex

effectiveness.design: Clinical field trial at 11 veterinary practices; positive control (lufenuron tablets, minimum 10 mg/kg once monthly) vs (S)-Methoprene minimum 22 mg/kg orally once weekly for 5 months in naturally flea-infested client-owned dogs; a topical adulticide mist was applied weekly for the first 8 weeks.
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Adult flea counts at months 0-5 and percent inhibition of fleas computed from geometric mean counts
effectiveness.result: (S)-Methoprene percent inhibition of fleas 73.5% (month 1), 87.5% (month 2), 85.7% (month 3), 89.8% (month 4), 92.8% (month 5) and 87.1% for months 1-5 combined, versus 85.6% for the lufenuron positive control; capsules worked as effectively as the positive control. Sixty-one of the 165 analysed dogs received (S)-Methoprene.
effectiveness.quote: A total of 246 (118 males, 127 females) dogs were enrolled in the study (the sex of one animal was not reported). Of these, 165 client owned dogs ranging in age from 6 months to 16 years and weighing between 4 to 130 pounds, were included in the statistical analysis. Sixty-one of the 165 dogs were treated with (S)-Methoprene.

adverse_reactions.term: Vomiting, diarrhea, lethargy/depression, nervousness (field trial, (S)-Methoprene group; no counts given)
adverse_reactions.quote: Vomiting, diarrhea, lethargy/depression and nervousness were observed in the (S)- Methoprene group.

adverse_reactions.term: Depression (target animal safety study, 6-week-old Beagle puppies; incidence by dose group)
Ataxia (target animal safety study, 6-week-old Beagle puppies; incidence by dose group)

adverse_reactions.quote: Tremors were exhibited in 1/6 and 1/4 dogs in the 1x and 10x treatment groups, respectively on day 0.

notes: Species not listed as a separate General Information field; 'Dogs' taken from the indication statement. Summary is an older (2000) format with no PK section. Effectiveness also supported by a dose-titration study (24 dogs; 20 mg/kg gave >90% reduction in adult flea emergence), a dose-confirmation study (20 dogs; 96.1% reduction at 22 mg/kg) and a 91-day simulated home environment study (20 dogs; 93.8% reduction in adult fleas by day 49). Field trial: 246 dogs enrolled, 165 analysed, 61 treated with (S)-Methoprene (the '61' is spelled out in the text so it is not in the n_dogs field). Target animal safety table rows were flattened by PDF extraction: for the depression and ataxia rows the successive fractions per dose group are the Day 0, Day 7, Day 14 (and for ataxia Day 21, Day 56) columns in order, with blank cells dropped; in the ataxia table the 3x row's last value (1/6) is the Day 56 column. Additional safety studies: 1-generation reproduction study at 3X in 52 Beagles (no drug-related effects except green-discoloured feces from capsule dye) and a 5X study in combination with topical flea adulticides in 24 puppies (no adverse effects).

indication.text: Dogs and cats: aid in controlling intractable animals during examination, treatment, grooming, x-ray and minor surgery; antipruritic; antiemetic for motion sickness; preanesthetic agent. Horses: aid in controlling fractious animals and adjunct to local anesthesia.
indication.quote: Acepromazine Maleate Injection can be used as an aid in controlling intractable animals during examination, treatment, grooming, x- ray and minor surgical procedures; to alleviate itching as a result of skin irritation; as an antiemetic to control vomiting associated with motion sickness.

dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: IV doses given slowly; allow at least 15 minutes for full effect. Cats 0.5-1 mg/lb; horses 2-4 mg/100 lb.

indication.text: Aid in tranquilization and preanesthetic agent in dogs; aid in controlling intractable animals during examination, treatment, grooming, x-ray and minor surgical procedures.
indication.quote: As an aid in tranquilization and as a preanesthetic agent in dogs. Acepromazine Maleate Tablets can be used as an aid in controlling intractable animals during examination, treatment, grooming, x-ray and minor surgical procedures.

dose_regimen.quote: 0.25 – 1.0 mg/lb of body weight. Dosage may be repeated as required.

pharmacokinetics.conditions: single oral 25 mg tablet, fasted, n=42 beagles, crossover; 90% CI; AUC from time 0 to last quantifiable concentration. Table columns: Generic mean, RLNAD mean, ratio, lower 90% CI, upper 90% CI.

single oral 25 mg tablet, fasted, n=42 beagles, crossover; 90% CI. Table columns: Generic mean, RLNAD mean, ratio, lower 90% CI, upper 90% CI.

single oral 25 mg tablet, fasted, n=42 beagles; TMAX summarized only, not statistically evaluated (NE = not estimated)

effectiveness.design: BIOEQUIVALENCE STUDY (not an effectiveness study): masked, randomized, two-period, two-sequence, single oral dose crossover blood-level study of generic 25 mg acepromazine maleate tablets vs RLNAD PromAce 25 mg tablets in healthy fasted male beagles, 7-day washout (Study 113-BC-2321, GLP).
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: CMAX and AUC; bioequivalence if 90% CI of the generic:RLNAD geometric mean ratio lies within 0.80-1.25
effectiveness.result: Bioequivalence demonstrated: AUC ratio 0.99 (90% CI 0.89-1.09), CMAX ratio 0.93 (90% CI 0.80-1.07). A biowaiver for the 10 mg tablet was granted on the basis of comparative in vitro dissolution (>85% in 15 minutes for all comparisons).
effectiveness.quote: The in vivo blood-level study was conducted in 42 healthy, fasted dogs.

adverse_reactions.quote: No serious adverse events were reported during the study.

notes: Generic (ANADA) approval; RLNAD is PromAce Tablets (NADA 117-532). No target animal safety or clinical effectiveness studies; the 'effectiveness' entry records the pivotal blood-level bioequivalence study. PK values are from Table II.1 (columns: Generic mean, RLNAD mean, Ratio, lower 90% CI, upper 90% CI; † geometric mean, ‡ arithmetic mean and SD). Study animals: 42 male beagles (41 intact, 1 neutered), 9.3-12.6 kg.

indication.text: Kills adult fleas; treatment and prevention of flea infestations (Ctenocephalides felis) and treatment and control of American Dog tick (Dermacentor variabilis) infestations for one month in dogs and puppies 8 weeks and older weighing 4 pounds or more.
indication.quote: NEXGARD kills adult fleas and is indicated for the treatment and prevention of flea infestations (Ctenocephalides felis), and the treatment and control of American Dog tick (Dermacentor variabilis) infestations in dogs and puppies 8 weeks of age and older, weighing 4 pounds of body weight or greater, for one month.

dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: chewable sizes 11.3, 28.3, 68 and 136 mg by body-weight band
dose_regimen.quote: NEXGARD is given orally once a month, at the minimum dosage of 1.14 mg/lb (2.5 mg/kg).

pharmacokinetics.value: 0.18 µg/mL mean plasma afoxolaner concentration 33 days post-treatment
pharmacokinetics.conditions: 2.5 mg/kg single oral dose of an experimental oral solution, fed (with an additional fasted group); first exploratory dose-ranging study; similar fed or fasted
pharmacokinetics.quote: Plasma concentrations averaged 0.18 µg/mL 33 days post-treatment at the 2.5 mg/kg dose level, and were similar under fed or fasted conditions.

pharmacokinetics.value: 0.18 µg/mL mean plasma concentration 33 days post-treatment
pharmacokinetics.conditions: 2.5 mg/kg single oral dose, second exploratory dose-ranging study
pharmacokinetics.quote: Plasma concentrations averaged 0.18 µg/mL 33 days post-treatment at the 2.5 mg/kg dose level.

pharmacokinetics.value: 0.1 µg/mL mean plasma concentration 28 days post-treatment
pharmacokinetics.conditions: 2.5 mg/kg single oral dose, third exploratory study in Beagles (0.75-3.5 mg/kg range)
pharmacokinetics.quote: The 2.5 mg/kg dosage maintained a 0.1 µg/mL mean plasma concentration 28 days post-treatment and an average of 99.8% effectiveness against fleas on day 31 post-treatment.

pharmacokinetics.value: plasma concentrations greater than 0.08 µg/ml were 100% effective against fleas (flea-effective concentration threshold)
pharmacokinetics.conditions: Beagles given single oral doses of 0.75, 1.5, 2.5 or 3.5 mg/kg (third exploratory study)
pharmacokinetics.quote: In the third study, Beagles administered a single oral dose of 0.75, 1.5, 2.5, or 3.5 mg/kg afoxolaner confirmed that plasma concentrations greater than 0.08 µg/ml were 100% effective against fleas.

pharmacokinetics.value: less than dose-proportional plasma afoxolaner concentrations after three monthly doses
pharmacokinetics.conditions: margin-of-safety study, 8-week-old Beagles, 1X/3X/5X of 6.3 mg/kg, pre-dose samples
pharmacokinetics.quote: Following the three monthly doses, plasma afoxolaner concentrations were less than proportional with dose administered.

pharmacokinetics.value: Day 125 plasma afoxolaner concentrations dose proportional up to 3X and more than dose proportional at 5X
pharmacokinetics.conditions: margin-of-safety study, after three doses every 2 weeks (Days 84, 98, 112) following three monthly doses
pharmacokinetics.quote: Following the three doses administered every 2 weeks, plasma afoxolaner concentrations on Day 125 were dose proportional up to 3X and more than dose proportional at 5X.

target_animal_safety.duration: three monthly treatments (Days 0, 28, 56) followed by three bi-weekly treatments (Days 84, 98, 112); six treatments per dog; necropsy Day 126

findings.finding: No deaths; no clinically relevant treatment-related changes in food consumption, body weight, physical examination, clinical pathology, gross pathology, histopathology or organ weights.
findings.quote: There were no deaths during the course of the study. There were no clinically relevant treatment-related changes in daily food consumption, body weight, physical examination variables, clinical pathology (hematology, clinical chemistries, or coagulation tests), gross pathology, histopathology, or organ weights.

findings.finding: Vomiting occurred throughout the study with similar incidence across all groups, including one 5X dog four hours after treatment.
findings.quote: Vomiting occurred throughout the study, with a similar incidence across all groups, including one dog in the 5X group that vomited four hours after treatment.

findings.finding: Conclusion: well tolerated in 8-week-old Beagles at 1, 3 or 5X the maximum exposure dose of 6.3 mg/kg for six doses.
findings.quote: Afoxolaner is well tolerated when administered to 8-week old Beagle dogs at 1, 3, or 5X the maximum potential exposure dose of 6.3 mg/kg at three, 28-day dose intervals followed by three, 2-week dose intervals for a total of 6 doses.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: 32 Beagle dogs (16 males, 16 females), 8 to 9 weeks of age, weighing between 2.3 and 4 kg.

effectiveness.design: Field study PR&D 02341: masked, multi-center (17 sites; 15 used for safety, 14 for effectiveness), randomized block, active-controlled (spinosad ≥30 mg/kg) study; NEXGARD ≥2.5 mg/kg orally once monthly for 3 consecutive months in households with natural flea infestations; 2:1 allocation NEXGARD:spinosad; flea counts on sentinel dogs at Days 0, 30, 60, 90.
effectiveness.n_dogs: 415 NEXGARD-treated and 200 spinosad-treated dogs (safety); 186 NEXGARD and 96 spinosad dogs in the Day 30 effectiveness analysis
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Percent reduction in geometric mean live flea counts on sentinel dogs compared with baseline (Visit 1) at Days 30, 60 and 90
effectiveness.result: Afoxolaner: 98.0% (Day 30), 99.7% (Day 60), 99.9% (Day 90) reduction vs baseline; spinosad: 95.7%, 99.4%, 99.7%; all reductions statistically significant (p<0.001). Both groups >90% effective; no conclusions on ticks (insufficient tick-infested dogs).
effectiveness.quote: 415 NEXGARD-treated dogs and 200 spinosad-treated dogs were evaluated for safety. The effectiveness analysis for Day 30 was performed on 186 NEXGARD-treated dogs and 96 spinosad-treated dogs.

adverse_reactions.term: Seizure in a dog with a history of seizures
adverse_reactions.quote: One dog with a history of seizures experienced a seizure on the same day after receiving the first dose and on the same day after receiving the second dose of NEXGARD.

notes: Original approval. PK data are limited to plasma-concentration statements from exploratory dose-ranging studies and the margin-of-safety study (no half-life, Cmax or AUC reported). Adverse reaction rows are from field study Table 8 (columns: Afoxolaner N, Afoxolaner % of n=415, Spinosad N, Spinosad % of n=200); a second dog with a seizure history seized nineteen days after the third dose. Laboratory dose-confirmation studies: fleas (32 dogs; 100% at 24 h post-infestation through Day 35, 81.1% at 12 h on Day 28) and two D. variabilis studies (16 dogs each; ≥97.3% and ≥98.5% at 48 h through Day 30). Target animal safety: study PR&D 0234001, treatment groups 0, 6.3 (1X), 18.9 (3X), 31.5 (5X) mg/kg.

indication.text: Supplement adds flea speed-of-kill language to the Effectiveness section of the package insert; indication unchanged (kills adult fleas; treatment and prevention of flea infestations; treatment and control of American Dog tick infestations for one month).
indication.quote: NEXGARD kills adult fleas and for the treatment and prevention of flea infestations (Ctenocephalides felis), and the treatment and control of American Dog tick (Dermacentor variabilis) infestations in dogs and puppies 8 weeks of age and older, weighing 4 pounds of body weight or greater, for one month.

dose_regimen.quote: NEXGARD is given orally, once a month, at the minimum dosage of 1.14 mg/lb (2.5 mg/kg).

effectiveness.design: Laboratory flea speed-of-kill study PR&D 0233403: untreated control vs single oral dose of NEXGARD (at least 2.5 mg/kg) on Day 0 after infestation with 100 fleas on Day -1; live fleas counted at 30 min, 2, 4, 8, 12 and 24 h (4 dogs/group/timepoint).
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Percent effectiveness against C. felis based on geometric mean live flea counts vs control at each timepoint
effectiveness.result: 0.0% at 30 minutes, 15.0% at 2 h, 87.8% at 4 h, 99.5% at 8 h, 100.0% at 12 and 24 h; significant vs control at 8, 12 and 24 h (P<0.005). NEXGARD started to kill fleas 4 hours after administration and demonstrated >99% effectiveness at 8 hours.
effectiveness.quote: 48 Beagle dogs (24 males, 24 females), 13.8 – 37.5 months of age, weighing between 7.1 – 14.8 kg.

adverse_reactions.quote: There were no adverse reactions during this study.

notes: Supplemental approval; CVM did not require target animal safety studies (refers to the original approval FOI Summary of September 14, 2013). Indication quote is verbatim from the General Information section, which omits 'is indicated' in this summary.

indication.text: Supplement adds treatment and control of Black-legged tick (Ixodes scapularis) and Lone Star tick (Amblyomma americanum) infestations for one month in dogs and puppies 8 weeks and older weighing 4 pounds or more.
indication.quote: NEXGARD kills adult fleas and is indicated for the treatment and prevention of flea infestations (Ctenocephalides felis), and the treatment and control of Black-legged tick (Ixodes scapularis), American Dog tick (Dermacentor variabilis), and Lone Star tick (Amblyomma americanum) infestations in dogs and puppies 8 weeks of age and older, weighing 4 pounds of body weight or greater, for one month.

dose_regimen.quote: NEXGARD is given orally, once a month at the minimum dosage of 1.14 mg/lb (2.5 mg/kg).

effectiveness.design: Four laboratory dose-confirmation studies (untreated control vs single oral dose ≥2.5 mg/kg on Day 0; weekly re-infestation with 50 ticks through Day 35): PR&D 0233301 and 0233303 for I. scapularis (48 h counts) and PR&D 0233106 and 0233109 for A. americanum (72 h counts). Quoted animals are from study PR&D 0233301.
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Percent reduction in geometric mean live tick counts vs control (control indication) and increase in dead tick counts (treatment indication) at 48 h (I. scapularis) or 72 h (A. americanum) after infestation
effectiveness.result: I. scapularis: ≥94.2% (study 0233301; 98.4, 99.1, 99.6, 94.2% on Days 2-30) and ≥98.0% (study 0233303; 20 dogs) effective through Day 30. A. americanum: ≥98.9% (study 0233106; 20 dogs) and ≥97.8% (study 0233109; 20 dogs) effective at 72 h through Day 30. Live tick counts significantly reduced and dead tick counts significantly increased vs control in all studies.
effectiveness.quote: 16 Beagle dogs (8 males, 8 females), 6.3 to 7.5 months of age, weighing between 5.2 – 8.7 kg

adverse_reactions.quote: There were no adverse reactions during this study.

notes: Supplemental approval; CVM did not require target animal safety studies (refers to the original approval FOI Summary of September 14, 2013). n_dogs refers to study PR&D 0233301 only; the other three studies enrolled 20 dogs each (10 per group). In study 0233301 two control dogs had reduced-vitality tick populations on Day 7, which compromised that timepoint only.

indication.text: Supplement adds treatment and control of Brown dog tick (Rhipicephalus sanguineus) infestations for one month in dogs and puppies 8 weeks and older weighing 4 pounds or more.
indication.quote: The effect of the supplement is to provide for the treatment and control of Brown dog tick (Rhipicephalus sanguineus) infestations in dogs and puppies 8 weeks of age and older, weighing 4 pounds of body weight or greater, for one month.

dose_regimen.quote: NEXGARD is given orally, once a month at the minimum dosage of 1.14 mg/lb (2.5 mg/kg).

effectiveness.design: Three laboratory dose-confirmation studies against induced adult R. sanguineus infestations (untreated control vs single oral dose ≥2.5 mg/kg on Day 0; weekly re-infestation with 50 ticks; live/dead tick counts at 48 h): PR&D 0233601 (South Africa; quoted animals), PR&D 0233004 (20 dogs) and PR&D 0233005 (20 dogs).
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Percent reduction in geometric mean live tick counts vs control at 48 h post-infestation through Day 30 (control indication); increased dead tick counts (treatment indication)
effectiveness.result: Study 0233601: ≥98.6% effective through Day 30 (100, 98.7, 99.3, 98.6, 99.3% on Days 2-30). Study 0233004 failed to demonstrate >90% effectiveness at Day 30 (83.9%). Study 0233005: ≥93.5% through Day 30. Combined average effectiveness 92.2% (>90%), which CVM accepted as demonstrating effectiveness for 30 days when assessed 48 h after administration or infestation.
effectiveness.quote: 16 Beagle dogs (7 males, 9 females), ≥ 6 months of age, weighing between 11.0-18.4 kg

adverse_reactions.quote: One dog had diarrhea within one day post-treatment; this dog had diarrhea one day prior to treatment as well. A second dog had diarrhea 12 and 24 days post-treatment.
There were no adverse reactions during this study.

notes: Supplemental approval; CVM did not require target animal safety studies (refers to the original approval FOI Summary of September 14, 2013). n_dogs refers to study PR&D 0233601 only.

indication.text: Supplement adds prevention of Borrelia burgdorferi infections as a direct result of killing Ixodes scapularis vector ticks.
indication.quote: NexGard® is indicated for the prevention of Borrelia burgdorferi infections as a direct result of killing Ixodes scapularis vector ticks.

dose_regimen.quote: NexGard® is given orally once a month at the minimum dosage of 1.14 mg/lb (2.5 mg/kg).

effectiveness.design: Laboratory study 0377501 (GCP): masked, randomized block; untreated control vs single oral NexGard dose (≥2.5 mg/kg) on Day 0; infestation on Day 28 with 50 wild-caught I. scapularis (63.1% B. burgdorferi infection rate); ticks counted/removed Day 33; serology (Lyme Quant C6, SNAP 4Dx) through Day 102 and PCR of 4 skin biopsies on Day 104. A second similar study (PR&D 0328901, 20 dogs) used serology only.
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Live tick counts on Day 33 and B. burgdorferi infection status (positive on either serology test or any skin-biopsy PCR)
effectiveness.result: All 10 NexGard dogs remained negative for B. burgdorferi by serology and PCR while all 10 control dogs became positive (p<0.0001); NexGard was 99.5% effective against wild-caught I. scapularis on Day 33. Second study: 0/10 treated vs 9/10 control dogs seropositive (p=0.0001), 100% tick effectiveness on Day 33.
effectiveness.quote: Study Animals: 20 Beagle dogs (10 males, 10 females), 6.7-8.0 months of age, weighing between 5.8-9.2 kg.

adverse_reactions.quote: There were no adverse reactions to NexGard® treatment.

notes: Supplemental approval; CVM did not require target animal safety studies (the summary's reference to 'NADA 141-460, dated September 13, 2013' appears to be a typo for NADA 141-406, September 14, 2013). No new PK data.

indication.text: Supplement provides a new modified formulation, adds treatment and control of Haemaphysalis longicornis (longhorned tick) infestations for one month, and adds label language on improvement of signs of flea allergy dermatitis as a direct result of eliminating fleas.
indication.quote: NexGard® kills adult fleas and is indicated for the treatment and prevention of flea infestations (Ctenocephalides felis), and the treatment and control of Ixodes scapularis (black-legged tick), Dermacentor variabilis (American dog tick), Amblyomma americanum (lone star tick), Rhipicephalus sanguineus (brown dog tick), and Haemaphysalis longicornis (longhorned tick) infestations in dogs and puppies 8 weeks of age and older, weighing 4 pounds of body weight or greater, for one month.

dose_regimen.quote: NexGard® is given orally once a month, at the minimum dosage of 1.14 mg/lb (2.5 mg/kg).

effectiveness.design: Field study PR&D 03547: active-controlled (oral spinosad), masked, multi-site (6 US sites), randomized block 3:1, three monthly oral treatments over 90 days in 103 households (178 dogs) with natural flea infestations and at least 2 signs of flea allergy dermatitis on the sentinel dog; flea counts and FAD sign scores on sentinel dogs at Days 30, 60, 90.
effectiveness.n_dogs: 121 NexGard-treated and 36 spinosad-treated dogs completed all four visits
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Percent effectiveness against fleas vs baseline at Days 30, 60, 90 (≥90% and significantly different from baseline); proportion of dogs with improved FAD signs (alopecia, erythema, papules, excoriation, scales/crusts)
effectiveness.result: NexGard ≥97.5% effective at every visit (97.5% Day 30, 99.7% Day 60, 99.9% Day 90; 63/63/59 dogs analysed); spinosad 93.2%, 97.9%, 99.3%. 70% of NexGard dogs showed improvement of individual FAD signs at Day 30, 87.8% at Day 60 and 91.1% at Day 90 (active control 53.3%, 81.8%, 81.3%). Longhorned tick laboratory studies PR&D 0434502 and 0434506 (20 dogs each): 98.5% and 100% effective 72/48 h after treatment and 100% at 72 h after weekly re-infestations through Day 31.
effectiveness.quote: One hundred twenty-one (121) dogs treated with NexGard® and 36 dogs treated with oral spinosad completed all four visits of the study.

notes: Supplemental approval; CVM did not require target animal safety studies (refers to the original approval FOI Summary of September 14, 2013); no PK data for the modified formulation are given in the summary. Adverse reaction rows are from field study Table II.9 (columns: NexGard N, NexGard % of n=130, active control N, active control % of n=46). Longhorned tick study tables were partly garbled by PDF extraction (e.g. '19. 5', a 'Study Day 34' row that is Day 24).

indication.text: Supplement adds treatment and control of Amblyomma maculatum (Gulf Coast tick) infestations for one month in dogs and puppies 8 weeks and older weighing 4 pounds or more.
indication.quote: This supplement provides for the addition of the indication for the treatment and control of Amblyomma maculatum (Gulf Coast tick) infestations in dogs and puppies 8 weeks of age and older, weighing 4 pounds of body weight or greater, for one month.

dose_regimen.quote: NexGard® is given orally once a month, at the minimum dosage of 1.14 mg/lb (2.5 mg/kg).

effectiveness.design: Two masked, negative-controlled laboratory dose-confirmation studies (GCP) with single oral NexGard dose (afoxolaner as close as possible to 2.5 mg/kg without under-dosing) on Day 0 and ~50 adult A. maculatum per infestation; live/dead tick counts 72 h after treatment or infestation. Study 2023-3557 (Colbert, GA; fed; infestations Days -1, 14, 28; quoted treatment groups) and Study 2024-3687 (South Africa; fasted; 20 dogs; infestations Days -2 to 35).
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Percent reduction (≥90%) in least-squares mean live tick counts vs control (control indication); numerically higher arithmetic mean dead ticks (treatment indication)
effectiveness.result: Study 2023-3557: ≥98.8% reduction in live A. maculatum at 72 h through Day 31 (99.5% Day 3, 100% Day 17, 98.8% Day 31; p<0.0001). Study 2024-3687: ≥94.6% through Day 38 (100, 97.7, 98.5, 98.9, 97.0, 94.6% on Days 3-38). Dead tick counts higher in treated dogs at all timepoints.

adverse_reactions.term: Diarrhea (study 2023-3557; considered a possible drug-related adverse reaction)
adverse_reactions.quote: One dog in the NexGard® treated group had a single incidence of diarrhea noted five hours after treatment.

dose_regimen.quote: NexGard® PLUS is given orally once a month at the minimum dosage of 1.14 mg/lb (2.5 mg/kg) afoxolaner, 5.45 mcg/lb (12 mcg/kg) moxidectin, and 2.27 mg/lb (5.0 mg/kg) pyrantel (as pamoate salt).

target_animal_safety.duration: six oral treatments 28 days apart (Days 0, 28, 56, 84, 112, 140); 168-day GLP study; necropsy Day 168

findings.finding: No test-article-related effects on food consumption, body weight, physical or ophthalmic examinations, or anatomical/clinical pathology; no signs of avermectin sensitivity.
findings.quote: There was no evidence of test article-related alterations in food consumption, body weight, physical examination variables (heart rate, respiratory rate, body temperature), ophthalmic examination variables, and anatomical or clinical pathology findings. No signs of avermectin sensitivity were observed.

findings.finding: Mild, self-limiting diarrhea (with and without blood) possibly treatment-related (more incidences in NexGard PLUS groups than control, including within 48 h of treatment).
findings.quote: Mild, self-limiting diarrhea (with and without blood) was observed sporadically and was possibly related to treatment, as there were more incidences in the groups administered NexGard® PLUS than the control group throughout the study, including within 48 hours after treatment.

findings.finding: Vomiting sporadic in all groups including control, not treatment-related.
findings.quote: Vomiting was observed sporadically across all groups, including the control group, and did not appear to be related to treatment.

findings.finding: Heartworm-positive dog study (PR&D 0430201; 1X and 3X, three doses ~28 days apart, 24 dogs): mild self-limiting diarrhea in one 1X and three 3X dogs, vomiting in two 3X dogs; no avermectin toxicity or hypersensitivity; microfilariae counts significantly lower than control.
findings.quote: Mild, self-limiting diarrhea was observed in one dog in the 1X group and in three dogs in the 3X group within 8 hours of treatment.

findings.finding: MDR1-deficient Collie study (PR&D 0423901; 1X, 3X, 5X; 24 dogs): no clinical signs of avermectin toxicity; vomiting in 3X and 5X groups within 8 h; self-limiting diarrhea in all treated groups.
findings.quote: No clinical signs of avermectin toxicity were noted in any dog at any time during the study. Vomiting was observed in the 3X and 5X groups within 8 hours of treatment and resolved without intervention.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: Study Animals: Thirty-two (32) Beagle dogs (16 males, 16 females), aged 8 to 9 weeks and weighing 1.95 to 3.00 kg, were included in the study.

effectiveness.design: Field study PR&D 04197 (GCP): masked, multicenter (6 US clinics in heartworm-endemic regions), randomized block, active-controlled (topical imidacloprid 10 mg/kg + moxidectin 2.5 mg/kg) heartworm-prevention study; owners administered NexGard PLUS monthly (12 treatments, Days 0-330) with or without food to heartworm-negative dogs; heartworm antigen and microfilariae testing Days 60, 120, 180, 240, 330.
effectiveness.n_dogs: 134 NexGard PLUS and 138 active control dogs (safety); 120 and 124 dogs (effectiveness)
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Heartworm antigen and blood microfilariae test results during 330 days (effectiveness shown if 100% negative; no statistical analysis then required)
effectiveness.result: 100% effectiveness: none of the 120 NexGard PLUS dogs tested positive for adult heartworms at any time point. Laboratory studies: 100% effective against induced D. immitis in two studies (PR&D 0409401, 0427201; 10 treated/10 control each, six monthly doses); 100%/≥99.8% against fleas (PR&D 0431501); 97-100% (≥98.4% after re-infestation) against A. americanum (PR&D 0424001, 0425701); effective against induced and naturally acquired T. canis (PR&D 0410401, 0426601).
effectiveness.quote: One hundred thirty-four (134) dogs administered NexGard® PLUS and 138 dogs administered the active control were evaluated for safety. One hundred twenty (120) dogs administered NexGard® PLUS and 124 dogs administered the active control were included in the effectiveness evaluation.

notes: Original approval of the three-way combination. No PK section in the summary (dosage characterization relies on prior NADA 141-406 and 140-971 data plus moxidectin exploratory studies at 3-100 mcg/kg; 12 mcg/kg x 6 monthly doses selected). Target animal safety from margin-of-safety study PR&D 0416301 (0X sham, 1X = 5 mg/kg afoxolaner + 24 mcg/kg moxidectin + 10 mg/kg pyrantel pamoate, 3X, 5X; 8 dogs/group; fasted). Adverse reaction rows are field study Table II.2 (NexGard PLUS n=134, active control n=138; anorexia 1 (0.7%) vs 4 (2.9%) omitted). The hookworm-specific laboratory studies were not reviewed in detail for this record.

effectiveness.design: Two masked, negative-controlled (sham-dosed), completely randomized laboratory studies (GCP): Study 2021083 (Athens, GA; quoted animals) and Study 2021084 (Colbert, GA; 20 dogs). Single oral NexGard PLUS dose (2.5 mg/kg afoxolaner, 12 mcg/kg moxidectin, 5 mg/kg pyrantel; fed) on Day 0; Day 28 infestation with ~50 wild-caught adult I. scapularis (60% and 38.5% B. burgdorferi infection rates); live tick counts Day 33; SNAP 4Dx Plus and Lyme Quant C6 serology through Day 103; PCR of 4 skin biopsies on Day 104.
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Percent reduction in arithmetic mean live tick counts on Day 33 and proportion of dogs infected with B. burgdorferi (any positive serology after Day 28 or positive biopsy PCR)
effectiveness.result: Both studies: 100% reduction in live I. scapularis on Day 33 (p<0.0001); 0/10 NexGard PLUS dogs vs 10/10 control dogs infected with B. burgdorferi (serology and PCR). A single dose 28 days before infestation prevented B. burgdorferi infection by killing the vector ticks.
effectiveness.quote: Study Animals: Twenty (20) beagle dogs (11 males and 9 females), 7.4 to 8.2 months of age and weighing 6.42 to 10.04 kg, were included in the study.
